cards.b: Every cell in your body holds about two metres of DNA, packed into a nucleus a few micrometres wide. It carries the recipe for you. Forensics, ancestry tests, vaccines and cancer drugs all begin here.

DNA is a long chain of nucleotides. Each has a sugar (deoxyribose), a phosphate and one of four bases: adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G), cytosine (C). The order of bases is the code.

Analogy: a ladder twisted into a spiral. Sugar-phosphate backbones are the rails; paired bases are the rungs.
Erwin Chargaff (1950) found that in any DNA, A equals T and G equals C in amount. This hinted at pairing: A-T by 2 hydrogen bonds, G-C by 3.
The two strands are antiparallel. One runs 5' to 3', the partner 3' to 5'. This matters for how DNA is copied.

1. Helicase unzips the helix at an origin, forming a fork.
  2. Primase lays a short RNA primer.
  3. DNA polymerase adds matching bases, only in the 5' to 3' direction.
  4. The leading strand is made smoothly; the lagging strand in pieces (Okazaki fragments, 1968).
  5. Ligase joins the pieces.

It is semi-conservative: each new helix has one old and one new strand. Polymerase also proofreads, with about one error in a billion bases.

cards.h: Packing two metres into a cell
cards.b: DNA wraps around proteins called histones, forming beads called nucleosomes. These coil into chromatin and then into chromosomes, visible during division. Humans have 3 billion base pairs per set of chromosomes. Prokaryotes keep a circular chromosome, plus small rings called plasmids that scientists later used as gene carriers.

Frederick Griffith (1928) saw bacteria transform. Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1944) showed the transforming substance was DNA. Hershey and Chase (1952) confirmed it with viruses. Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image (Photo 51, 1952) and Maurice Wilkins's data helped Watson and Crick propose the double helix in 1953 (Nobel 1962 to Watson, Crick, Wilkins). Meselson and Stahl (1958) proved semi-conservative copying.

Fix these

  • A gene is not the whole DNA; it is a stretch of it.
  • DNA is not the same as a chromosome; chromosomes are DNA wrapped on proteins.
  • Franklin's contribution is often understated.

Har Gobind Khorana (born in Raipur, now Pakistan, 1922) chemically synthesised the first artificial gene in 1970 and shared the 1968 Nobel for cracking the genetic code. At CCMB, Hyderabad, Lalji Singh developed DNA fingerprinting in India, used in forensic and paternity cases. The GenomeIndia project has sequenced 10,000 Indian genomes (announced 2025).

• DNA is a double helix of four bases; A-T, G-C.
  • Replication is semi-conservative: helicase, primase, polymerase, ligase.
  • Griffith to Hershey-Chase proved DNA is the genetic material.

Think about it:

  1. If one strand reads ATGC, what is the other?
  2. Why is semi-conservative copying good for accuracy?
